analysis: What changed versus the 4 AM PT brief: the pre-open bank wave resolved into real prints, and it split three ways. (1) BAC confirmed the worst of it: even excluding the $1.2B Treasury AML fine, EPS of $1.08 missed the $1.10 consensus and revenue came up short, with the bank acknowledging willful Bank Secrecy Act violations — shares -4% premarket. (2) MS and BLK were clean beats — MS's +41% equities line and record wealth revenue, BLK's $205B inflows and $15.49T AUM — but only BLK is getting paid for it premarket (+3-4%) while MS wavers near flat, which reads as a tape that is holding its breath for CPI in 30 minutes. (3) State Street's mixed print (EPS beat, revenue miss) selling toward a three-month low says the market is punishing anything less than clean. The AI complex stays two-track: ASML's 2030 order-interest comments held Amsterdam +3%, but U.S. memory names keep bleeding (MU -1.25%, SNDK -2.4%, SK Hynix -3%) on the still-unsubstantiated CXMT claim. CPI at 5:30 AM PT (core +0.2% m/m expected) now decides whether the 10Y's -3bp drift and the calm futures tape get validated or repriced. Signal vs noise: BAC/MS/BLK prints are confirmed via WSJ, Reuters, Barron's; STT details rest on one outlet so far; the CXMT 4F2 breakthrough claim remains explicitly unconfirmed — treat the memory selloff as fragile by definition. No qualifying HN/Reddit threads — community channels were silent on today's stories.

headlines.headline: Bank of America Q3: net income $6.9B vs $8.3B a year ago; diluted EPS 91c including the $1.2B Treasury AML fine, or $1.08 ex-charge vs $1.10 consensus; revenue just shy of $30B vs $30.58B expected. NII rose 8% YoY to $16.4B. Shares -4% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: A miss even before the fine — adjusted EPS still came up short and revenue missed, and the bank acknowledged willful Bank Secrecy Act violations, raising governance and future-scrutiny risk — so the tape is pricing both the number and the control failures.

headlines.headline: Morgan Stanley Q3: beat — net income $4.97B (+7% YoY), EPS $3.03 vs $2.93 expected; revenue $20.34B vs $19.93B. Equities revenue +41% to $5.79B, wealth management record $9.07B (+10%), investment banking +2% to $2.16B, fixed income -7%; ROTCE 22.6%. Shares wavering near flat premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The cleanest bank print of the morning — trading and wealth both delivered — but the stock getting no lift says the market is parked for CPI, so this beat's follow-through depends on the 5:30 AM PT print.

headlines.headline: BlackRock Q3: beat — adjusted EPS $15.93 (+38% YoY) vs $14.32 expected; revenue $7.75B (+19%) vs $7.42B; AUM $15.49T (+15%, ~half of U.S. GDP) on $205B net inflows, $135B into iShares. Shares +3-4% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Beat on both lines with the strongest inflow print in the group — the one premarket winner of the morning wave, as fee income is treated as shelter from the NII/fine tape elsewhere in financials.

headlines.headline: State Street Q3: edged past EPS expectations but slightly missed on revenue (per IBD live coverage). Shares fell sharply premarket, eyeing a three-month low.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-outlet detail so far — treat as fragile until the release — but the premarket drop says anything short of clean is getting sold into the CPI window.

headlines.headline: ASML follow-through: Amsterdam shares +3%, U.S. ADRs wavering around flat premarket; Citi says the real takeaway is customer interest in securing capacity for 2029-2030. U.S. memory names still bleeding — MU -1.25% to $941.31, SNDK -2.4%, SK Hynix -3%, INTC -1%+. Barclays cut HPE and DELL to Equal Weight (HPE -4%, DELL -3% premarket).
headlines.why_it_matters: Equipment demand is being confirmed by the vendor while memory keeps selling off — the two-track tape says the CXMT supply-scare (still unconfirmed) is overriding ASML's demand evidence in U.S. memory names.

headlines.headline: September CPI lands at 8:30 AM ET (5:30 AM PT), 30 minutes after this brief: consensus 3.6% y/y headline (from 3.4%), +0.6% m/m, core +0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y. FedWatch: ~22% chance of an October hike, ~89% for a December hike.
headlines.why_it_matters: The core monthly print is the decider — ~0.2% keeps the Fed on hold and validates the calm futures tape, ~0.3% revives October hike bets and reprices bonds and stocks instantly; carried from the 4 AM brief.

headlines.headline: Macro cross-currents: China's September imports +31.0% y/y vs +24.5% expected; Brent near $106/bbl, European gas near four-year highs; Japan's 5Y JGB auction cleared stronger (bid-to-cover 3.56x); 10Y Treasury near 5.20%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Strong China imports are a demand positive for global growth, but energy inflation at these levels is exactly what keeps the Fed hawkish — a reminder that CPI's energy read matters as much as core.
